origin.description: glue with crayon style names written in the brace.

arguments.name: parts
arguments.text: Template. {blue foo} colors the word foo.

arguments.name: literal
arguments.text: When true, quotes and # inside a style brace are ordinary characters.

origin.details: The first word is a crayon function. The rest is glued again, so styles can nest.
origin.value: A character vector of class glue, containing ANSI sequences.
origin.example: cat(as.character(glue_col("{red This is a {green serious} problem}")), "\n", sep = "")

translation.description: glue with the same style names. The ANSI codes are the ones crayon emits.

arguments.name: parts
arguments.text: Template. {blue foo} colors the word foo.

arguments.name: literal
arguments.text: When true, quotes and # inside a style brace are ordinary characters.

translation.details: The first word selects a style. Nested braces are glued again. A close code inside the text is replaced by the outer open code, which is how crayon nests colors. rich is not used.
translation.value: A Glue vector containing the same ANSI sequences.
translation.example:
from glue import glue_col
print(glue_col("{red This is a {green serious} problem}", envir={}))
